title: Wisdom
english: …King David, now an elder, had advanced in years and conducted his life in a way that was beyond reproach. He had struggled against his enemies and emerged victorious, increasing his power and becoming invulnerable to those who plotted against him. Not only had he defeated foreign nations, but he had also turned back the barbarian hordes and overcome those who rose up against him at the right time, as well as those who conspired with them. King David's example teaches us that we should ask God for a heart that can hear and discern His will, so that we may serve Him wisely, being knowledgeable about what is beneficial, vigilant in our minds toward those who use us, and willing to calm the storms of this present life.

Just as a ship with rudders can navigate through treacherous waters and avoid the attacks of the waves, even when the sea is raging, so too can a person's soul, governed by good thoughts and wisdom, escape the raging Satan and render useless the evil plots against it. But a heart without wisdom will hardly endure the challenges of life, and will be easily wrecked on the rocks of circumstance. It is for this reason that Solomon's request for wisdom was pleasing to the Lord, and he was deemed worthy of the gift. For God willingly grants wisdom to those who ask for it with a pure heart.

The most exceptional gift from God is wisdom, accompanied by understanding, which illuminates even the nature of angels and the blessed multitude of spirits in heaven. This gift is truly precious and surpasses all other possessions that could be of benefit to the human soul. For what other possession could compare to the value of wisdom and knowledge of God? Certainly not gold or silver, which are temporary and useless, providing no benefit to the human soul.

The divine Scripture teaches us what to ask for and what to receive as an addition to our requests. For when we ask for wisdom, all other things are added to it, as stated in the Gospels: Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you (Matthew 6:33). This is why we should let our eyes and ears be opened to the things of God, and understand that the Scripture speaks to us in terms of what we know and have experienced, due to our poverty of mind and tongue, for things about God are entirely unspeakable.
Those who are embodied in coarse and thick bodies are unable to understand the necessities, unless they are in a state of order…
